title: Electron 36 fails to launch because "Using GTK 2/3 and GTK 4 in the same process is not supported"
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

36.0.0-alpha.1 through 36.0.0-beta.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

23.10

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

35.*

### Expected Behavior

When running Fiddle on Ubuntu with X11, launching the default template works

### Actual Behavior

Launching the default template using any of the current 36.X beta and alpha releases fails with the following error:

```
Electron v36.0.0-alpha.1 started.
(process:12023): Gtk-ERROR **: 11:30:38.382: GTK 2/3 symbols detected. Using GTK 2/3 and GTK 4 in the same process is not supported

Electron exited with signal SIGTRAP.
```

### Testcase Gist URL

Default fiddle template shows this

### Additional Information

_No response_

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
setting `gtk-version=3` works for me. For other people encountering this thread, you can pass it at a command line argument, and you can also set that in your main init script:

```js
app.commandLine.appendSwitch('gtk-version', '3');
```

comments.author: participant16
comments.body:
The issue was added to the release notes of electron 36

https://<redacted-host>/blog/electron-36-0#behavior-changed-gtk-4-is-the-default-when-running-on-gnome

>Behavior Changed: GTK 4 is the default when running on GNOME
After an upstream change, GTK 4 is now the default when running on GNOME.
In rare cases, this may cause some applications or configurations to error with the following message:
`Gtk-ERROR **: 11:30:38.382: GTK 2/3 symbols detected. Using GTK 2/3 and GTK 4 in the same process is not supported`
Affected users can work around this by specifying the gtk-version command-line flag:
`$ electron --gtk-version=3   # or --gtk-version=2`
The same can be done with the app.commandLine.appendSwitch function.

comments.author: participant22
comments.body:
This might be a little off-topic but while  `--gtk-version=3` (not 4) let me launch the process - it doesn't seem to properly extend to subprocesses that electron creates;   Calling `webContents.print()` produces a GTK warning for me and prevents the print dialog from opening.  (I will note that executing "window.print()" in the view works fine without warnings; but this is not ideal in our case.)

```
(process:2645): Gtk-ERROR **: 11:43:34.441: GTK 2/3 symbols detected. Using GTK 2/3 and GTK 4 in the same process is not supported.
```

Last week this also came with a message of a subprocess crashing with child-process-gone, but this week I can't reproduce the crash message on the same versions and hardware.
Because of the inability to reliably call webContents.print in v36, we are downgrading to 35 though.


Some system information:
Oracle Linux 9.6 (redhat/fedora-based)
Running under mutter/wayland with gnome-kiosk-script-session
Seems to have GTK4 and GTK3 installed as dependencies of gdm and gnome-kiosk respectively.  When I test installing gnome-kiosk, both 3 and 4 get installed.  Removing either will remove gdm and/or gnome-kiosk.

gdm.x86_64  1:40.1-28.0.1.el9_6  ol9_appstream
gnome-kiosk 40.0-7
mutter 40.9-24
libwayland-* 1.21.0
gtk3 3.24.31-5
gtk4 4.12.3-2
